newsitem.title: USA: German tourist found dead in Yosemite.
newsitem.headline: German tourist found dead in Yosemite.

text.p: The body of a man believed to be a German tourist has been found at the bottom of a cliff in California's Yosemite National Park where he apparently fell to his death, park officials said on Friday.
The 29-year-old man, whose name was not released, apparently fell about 2,000 ft (600 metres) from the top of Half Dome mountain some time around July 5, a statement from the national park said.
The man is believed to have hiked to the top of the mountain, said officials at Yosemite, 150 miles (240 kms) southeast of San Francisco.

The partially decomposed body was found on Wednesday evening by two climbers at the base of Half Dome. The climbers alerted park rangers and a search and rescue team hiked to the scene where they found the body in a scree-filled gully. The body was airlifted out on Thursday afternoon, the park said.
Items found at the scene enabled investigators to make a preliminary identification of the victim.
Park rangers were working with the German consulate in San Francisco to notify the man's family.

Investigators found a park entrance receipt from July 5, suggesting the man may have died on that date. He had not been registered as a guest at any accommodation in the park and had not been reported missing to park authorities.
The German consulate in San Francisco declined comment.
